newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds end weaker but outperform U.S. issues.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds end weaker but outperform U.S. issues.

text.p: Canadian bonds pared early gains to close weaker on Tuesday, but outperformed U.S. issues as markets in both countries weakened on concern about a possible rise in U.S. interest rates, analysts said.

"It's just been a slow grind lower really in tandem with the U.S. market," said Harvinder Kalirai, Canadian analyst with New York-based financial analysis firm I.D.E.A. "The Canadian dollar is strengthening up a little bit, so that's giving support."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.25 to C$110.60 to yield 7.101 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond rose 14/32 to yield 6.92 percent. The spread between the bonds narrowed to 18 basis points from 20 basis points at the close of trading on Monday.
"I think this is all U.S.-driven. Canada has got superior fundamentals," said Hank Cunningham, director of fixed income with First Marathon Securities Ltd.

Canadian and U.S. fixed-income markets opened stronger today after the U.S. Commerce Department said retail sales fell 0.3 percent in April and fell 0.1 percent less auto sales. Sales were expected to fall 0.3 percent overall and rise 0.1 percent less auto sales.

But Canadian and U.S. bond markets pared gains after the report as traders sold into the rally. Losses deepened in the afternoon on a Reuters story citing an unnamed source near the U.S. Federal Reserve saying odds favored a May rate hike.
The Fed's rate-setting Open Market Committee meets on May 20 to decide whether to hike U.S. rates a second time this year. A U.S. rate hike would likely weigh on Canadian bonds and the currency.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.15 to C$103.05 to yield 6.564 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond fell 12/32 to yield 6.71 percent.
The negative spread between the two bonds widened to 15 basis points from 11 basis points at Monday's close.
The three-month cash T-bill traded with a yield of 3.09 percent against its U.S. equivalent, which yielded 5.21 percent.
